evals.prompt: eval-inputs/product-on-gray.png in Compositor's Agent folder is a product shot on a flat gray backdrop. I need a transparent PNG cutout of just the product, trimmed with 20 px of padding, saved as out/product-cutout.png. Keep a layered .comp too, with the original photo recoverable.
evals.expected_output: Opens or imports the image, isolates the product with remove_background or a color selection of the backdrop turned into a mask, checks the edge at 100% over a contrasting background, applies the mask (or keeps it and exports), trims with padding 20, exports a transparent PNG, and saves a .comp in which the original pixels are still available (a mask not yet applied, or a hidden duplicate).
expectations: out/product-cutout.png exists, is a PNG with an alpha channel, and is 640 x 640 pixels within 6 px (the 600 px product plus 20 px padding on each side)
In out/product-cutout.png the corner pixel (0, 0) has alpha 0 and the center pixel has alpha 255 with a red color (r > 0.7, g < 0.3, b < 0.3)
The transcript shows remove_background, or select_by_color on the backdrop followed by add_layer_mask (or clear_selection on a duplicate), rather than painting the background away by hand
A .comp was saved whose document still holds the original gray backdrop pixels: a layer with an unapplied mask, or a hidden copy of the original layer
The transcript shows a render (render_layer or render_region) of the cutout's edge before export

evals.prompt: eval-inputs/dim-warm-room.png in Compositor's Agent folder is too dark and far too orange. Fix the exposure and the color cast, keep it adjustable so I can dial it back later, and export out/room-corrected.jpg in the Agent folder.
evals.expected_output: Measures with sample_colors, adds adjustment layers (Levels, Curves or Exposure for brightness; Color Balance, Curves per channel or Hue/Saturation for the cast) instead of filtering the pixels, re-samples to confirm the image is brighter and more neutral, exports a JPEG and saves a .comp with the adjustment layers.
expectations: out/room-corrected.jpg exists and is 1600 x 1067 pixels
The mean luminance of out/room-corrected.jpg is higher than that of eval-inputs/dim-warm-room.png (checked with a short Pillow script)
The mean red minus mean blue of out/room-corrected.jpg is smaller than in eval-inputs/dim-warm-room.png
A saved .comp contains at least one adjustment layer (kind adjustment) and the photo layer's own pixels match the input (psd-diff.py between the input and the layer's image passes)
The transcript shows sample_colors (or get_pixel_color) before the first adjustment and again after the last

evals.prompt: Give eval-inputs/city-street.png (in Compositor's Agent folder) a film look with one of Adobe's Film-Inspired Lightroom profiles at about 70% strength, export out/city-film.jpg in the Agent folder, and tell me which profile you picked.
evals.expected_output: Lists profiles (list_profiles with a query or group for the film profiles), picks a usable one that supports amount, adds a Profile adjustment layer with amount 70 (clipped to the photo when needed), renders to check, exports the JPEG, and names the profile and its fidelity in the answer.
expectations: The transcript shows list_profiles with a query or group before the profile layer is added
The transcript shows add_adjustment_layer with kind 'profile' and settings amount 70 (or set_adjustment setting amount 70 afterwards), with a profile whose supports_amount is true
out/city-film.jpg exists and is 1500 x 1000 pixels, and differs from the input (psd-diff.py reports differing pixels)
The final answer names the chosen profile (its name or Group/Name) and says whether its fidelity is exact or approximate
